AvailableScopeListEntry.description: An entry in the list of available scopes

builtin.description: Whether this is a built-in or a custom scope

contactEmail.description: Email, which can be used to announce breaking changes. Can be a semicolon separated list. Make sure this is always up-to-date so we can reach you on important topics!

name.description: Name for the idp-client. Unique per service-instance. Can NOT be changed later.

protocol.description: Determines if this is an oidc or saml-client

realm.description: Authentication-Realm in which the client exists. Different realms have different global settings.

ClientKPI.description: A single KPI for a client

unit.description: The unit the value is in

value.description: The current numerical value for this KPI

claimName.description: Name of the claim to set

value.description: Value to set for the claim

valueType.description: As which data-type to set the value

claimName.description: Name of the claim to set

userAttribute.description: User attribute to take the value from

valueType.description: As which data-type to set the value

attributeFriendlyName.description: Friendly Name of the attribute to set

attributeName.description: Name of the attribute to set

nameFormat.description: As which data-type to set the value

value.description: Value to set for the claim

attributeFriendlyName.description: Friendly Name of the attribute to set

attributeName.description: Name of the SAML attribute to map to

nameFormat.description: As which data-type to set the value

userAttribute.description: User attribute to take the value from

Scope.description: An OAUTH2-Scope, which allows an application to perform actions in another application on behalf of a user

audiences.description: A list of clientIDs that should be included in the aud-claim of the access-token if this scope is used

description.description: What this scope does and for who it is intended

realm.description: Realm in which the scope exists

accessType.description: When public, no clientsecret is required to perform logins using this client. Clients that have the Client Credentials Flow enabled can not be public.

adminURL.description: URL to the admin interface of the client. Set this if the client supports the adapter REST API. This REST API allows the auth server to push revocation policies and other administrative tasks. Usually this is set to the base URL of the client.

authorizationCodeFlowEnabled.description: Enable the [authorization code flow](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/oidc-conformant-authentication/oidc-adoption-auth-code-flow) for this client. The standard and preferred Oauth/OIDC-Flow.

baseURL.description: Default URL to use when the auth server needs to redirect or link back to the client.

clientCredentialsFlowEnabled.description: Enable the [client credentials flow](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/client-credentials-flow). Used for machine-to-machine Authentication. (Can not be enabled for public clients).

clientID.description: The clientId, as used for OAUTH-Flows.

clientSecret.description: The clientSecret, as used for OAUTH-Flows.

defaultClientScopes.description: Default client scopes are always applied when issuing tokens for this client. Scope mappings are always applied regardless of value of used scope parameter in OIDC Authorization request.

deviceAuthorizationFlowEnabled.description: Enable the [device authorization flow](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/device-authorization-flow). Used when the device that needs authentication does not have a suitable browser (Smart-Devices, CLI-Tools etc.).

discoveryURL.description: The OIDC-Discovery-URL for this client. Used to automatically configure most OIDC-Client-Applications.

hardcodedClaimMappers.description: Hardcoded Mappers can be used to set a claim in the ID token & userinfo-endpoint (NOT to the access token) to a fixed value.

implicitFlowEnabled.description: Enable the [implicit flow](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/oidc-conformant-authentication/oidc-adoption-implicit-flow). Has historically been used for frontend-applications that can't keep a clientSecret confidential. DEPRECATED! Use Authorization Code Flow with PKCE instead if possible!

optionalClientScopes.description: Optional client scopes are applied when issuing tokens for this client when they are requested by scope parameter in OIDC Authorization request.

rootURL.description: Root URL appended to relative URLs.

validRedirectURIs.description: Allowed redirect URIs for authorization code flow. Supports custom schemes. HTTP-URLs (no TLS) are only allowed for the domain "localhost". You can use a '*' as wildcard at the end of a string. (If you don't have/need a redirect URI, just disable the authorization code flow below)

webOrigins.description: Allowed CORS origins. Enter the string "+" to automatically treat all validRedirectURIs as allowed CORS origins. Required when doing Token-Requests from Clientside-Javascript.

baseURL.description: Default URL to use when the auth server needs to redirect or link back to the client.

canoncializationMethod.description: Canonicalization method which should be used.

clientSignatureRequired.description: Will the client sign their saml requests and responses? And should they be validated?

clientSigningCertificate.description: Base64 encoded client signing certificate without any spaces. Request-Signatures will be validated using this.

defaultClientScopes.description: Default client scopes are always applied when issuing tokens for this client. Scope mappings are always applied regardless of value of used scope parameter in OIDC Authorization request.

encryptAssertion.description: Should SAML assertions be encrypted with client's public key using AES?

encryptionCertificate.description: Base64 encoded client encryption certificate without any spaces

entityIdentifier.description: UNIQUE identifier for this SAML-Client. It is recommended that a system entity use a URL containing its own domain name to identify itself and avoid collisions.

forceNameIDFormat.description: Ignore requested Name ID subject format and use Name ID format configured below.

forcePostBinding.description: Always use POST binding for responses.

hardcodedAttributeMappers.description: Hardcoded Mappers can be used to set an attribute in the SAML response to a fixed value.

includeAuthnStatement.description: Should a statement specifying the method and timestamp be included in login responses?

logoutPostBindingURL.description: SAML POST Binding URL for the client's single logout service. You can leave this blank if you are using a different binding.

logoutRedirectBindingURL.description: SAML Redirect Binding URL for the client's single logout service. You can leave this blank if you are using a different binding.

metadataURL.description: The URL where you can download the SAML-Metadata for your client. Used for auto-configuration of client-applications.

nameIDFormat.description: Name ID Format which should be used.

postBindingURL.description: SAML POST Binding URL for the client's assertion consumer service (login responses). You can leave this blank if you do not have a URL for this binding.

predefinedMappers.description: Mappers allow you to add additional user attributes to the SAML response. These are predefined mappers for the most common use-cases.

redirectBindingURL.description: SAML Redirect Binding URL for the client's assertion consumer service (login responses). You can leave this blank if you do not have a URL for this binding.

rootURL.description: Root URL appended to relative URLs.

signAssertion.description: Should assertions inside SAML documents be signed? This setting is not needed if document is already being signed.

signDocuments.description: When turned on, Cloud IDP will sign the document using the realm’s private key.

ssoURLName.description: URL fragment name to reference client when you want to do IDP Initiated SSO.

userAttributeMappers.description: User Attribute Mappers allow you to add additional user attributes to the SAML response. Use these custom mappers if no predefined mapper fits your use-case.

validRedirectURIs.description: Allowed redirect URIs for SAML-Logins. Supports custom schemes. HTTP-URLs (no TLS) are only allowed for the domain "localhost". You can use a '*' as wildcard at the end of a string. Required when Authorization Code Flow is enabled.
